summary: CENTRA-G is a hybrid system that combines a short-radius centrifuge with exercise equipment and a real-time simulation function to help maintain astronauts’ physical health during long-duration space missions. By performing cycling and squats simultaneously in a rotating environment, the system aims to provide gravitational loading, circulatory stimulation, and aerobic exercise in a single session. It is designed to address health issues associated with microgravity, including bone density loss, muscle atrophy, and fluid shifts. The system also includes a real-time simulator that allows users to monitor and adjust physical parameters. With an estimated mass of 300 kg or less and continuous power consumption of 650 W or less, CENTRA-G aims to support astronauts’ physical function during future lunar and Mars exploration missions.
details:
1. What does the project do? It is a hybrid system of short-radius centrifuges and exercise and a health decision support workspace to prevent health damage (bone density loss, muscle atrophy, fluid shift, etc.) caused by the microgravity environment in long-term spaceflight.

2. How does it work? Cycle ergometer and squat are performed at the same time in the centrifuge aircraft of the semi-queenvent (semi-lying position) position that generates 1.0G at the foot at a foot radius of 2.0m and a rotational speed of 21.1rpm. It also has a simulator function that allows you to operate and check physical parameters in real time.

3. What are the advantages? It complements the "leg-pulling gravity load" that cannot be reproduced by ISS's existing exercise equipment, and can efficiently achieve gravity load, circulatory stimulation, and aerobic exercise simultaneously in one session.

4. What is the intended impact of the project? It is to prevent the decline of astronauts' physical function and standing resistance in future long-term missions and lunar and Martian explorations, and to provide a reliable design basis for ground bed rest tests and future flight demonstrations.

5. Tools, programming languages, hardware, and software used for development

UI / Language: HTML, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS (CDN), Inter, Orbitron

Data visualization: Chart.js (v4.4.1), native SVG

System estimate: mass $\le 300\text{ kg}$ or less, continuous power $\le 650\text{ W}$ or less (about 260-325Wh per 30-minute session)

6. What is the creativity of the project? It is based on an integrated approach that performs centrifuges and movement at the same time in a rotating gravity gradient environment, and a structure that clearly separates and opens the calculated values and assumptions based on the physical model of the NASA NTRS official technical document.

7. What factors did the team consider? We considered a comparative study of folding arms, etc. for ISS accommodation, anti-torque and vibration offset by coaxial reverse rotation mass, step-by-step familiarization protocols and emergency stop mechanisms, and ethical data design without automatic diagnosis.
